ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, the graph of the linear function $y=x+3$, denoted by ${l}_{1}$, intersects the $x$-axis at point $B$, and intersects the graph of another linear function passing through point $A(3, 0)$, denoted by ${l}_{2}$, at point $C(1, m)$. What is the equation of the linear function represented by the graph ${l}_{2}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $C(1, m)$ is on the graph of $l_1\colon y=x+3$,\\
$\therefore m=1+3=4$;\\
Assume the expression for the linear function graph $l_2$ is $y=kx+b\ (k\ne 0)$,\\
Substituting the points $A(3, 0)$ and $C(1, 4)$, we get: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}3k+b=0 \\ k+b=4\end{array}\right.$,\\
Solving this, we find $\left\{\begin{array}{l}k=-2 \\ b=6\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ The equation of $l_2$ is: \boxed{y=-2x+6}.
